title: Reified RSpaces: the conformance of each normative clause of the FIPS

fips.title: Agents
fips.outside: Lines 1 to 7 (the title), 59 to 131 (the example) and 133 to 138 (contracts as agents)

spec_holes.hole: The surface syntax of similarity queries and of params
spec_holes.resolution: The syntax contract gives send params and receive queries as the protobuf fields `Send.params` and `ReceiveBind.query_spec`. The VectorDB family takes the query keys of rule VD-3.

spec_holes.hole: The theory documents, which a later design document was to specify
spec_holes.resolution: The theory seam admits the builtin structural theories now. The MeTTaIL theories come through the seam in phase P12.

spec_holes.hole: The unification question of the quantale section
spec_holes.resolution: The passage is informative, and follow-up rrs-fu-quantale-unification routes the question to the FIPS authors.

spec_holes.hole: Tensor logic and nonlinear vector operations, which the FIPS marks as topics to look into
spec_holes.resolution: The design study of decision 52 answered the question. Tensor logic and the nonlinear operations come in phase P12.

rows.clause: The title, the authors, the date and the abstract of the FIPS.
rows.reason: The abstract summarizes the clauses of the rows RR-04 (the invariant), RR-05 (the agent) and RR-13 to RR-28 (the stores and the collections).

rows.clause: Background: the four groups of operations of the ISpace trait of the baseline (checkpoints, replay, produce and consume).
rows.reason: The section describes the baseline. The campaign does not change ISpace, and the substrate reaches the same operations through SpaceTxnHost.

rows.clause: An RSpace is a key-value store: a channel or a group of channels is a key, a data bag and a continuation bag are the value, and a channel exists on its first use.
rows.note: Each collection of a space holds its records and its waiters, and its first operation opens it (rule OC-2).

rows.clause: The invariant: after each produce or consume, no data and no continuation match, and every generalization keeps the invariant.
rows.note: On a head-only collection the invariant concerns the heads: a head that does not match blocks the entries behind it (decision 11).

rows.clause: Every agent with the behavioral type of a space can be an RSpace, and every RSpace can be reified into an agent.
The constructor takes a qualifier (default, temp or seq), a theory and more arguments, and it may abort when it does not support the qualifier.
The theory of a space is a MeTTaIL theory that describes the data of its channels.
rows.note: The builtin structural theories Nat, Int, String, Bool and Any work now (row RR-06). The MeTTaIL theories come through the theory seam in phase P12, after the readiness signal of F1r3lang.

rows.clause: The method gensym returns a name, and it may abort, for example when it runs out of names.
The method produce sends a process on a channel, and it may abort, for example when the process holds a Seq name.
The method consume receives on a join: pairs of a matcher and a channel, the arrow <-, <= or <<-, and a body that takes a map of the bindings.
Patterns will grow into spatial-behavioral types in datalog form, and matchers will then tailor patterns to the inner structure and the theory.
rows.reason: The sentence states a direction of future pattern work and requires no behavior of this version.

rows.clause: The namespace rho:space holds combinations of stores and collections, and developers can write their own spaces.
The outer store HashMap, the store of the current implementation.
The outer store PathMap: channels are paths, a send also sends on every prefix, and a receive on a prefix binds the re-rooted data and leaves the rest.
rows.note: Lines 181 to 183 of the FIPS write the pathmaps without their opening bar, for example {[2, "hello"], [3, "there"]|}. The rows read them as pathmaps.

rows.clause: The quantale semantics of sequential processes on sets of paths.
rows.reason: The FIPS states the semantics with an open question on line 193. Decision 87 records it as informative, and follow-up rrs-fu-quantale-unification routes it to the FIPS authors.

rows.clause: The outer store Array of fixed length: new gives the next index up to the maximum, then aborts with an out-of-names error, and indices can be unforgeable.
rows.note: Each index name is an unforgeable id of its space, so a client cannot reach an index ambiently (rule AR-1).

rows.clause: The outer store Array with reuse: new gives the next index modulo the size.
The outer store Vector of unbounded length: new grows the vector and gives the index of its last element, and indices can be unforgeable.
When the server runs out of memory, the deploy fails with an out-of-memory error.
rows.note: A deploy fails deterministically when it exceeds its phlo or its host-work budget. Memory exhaustion cannot be a consensus outcome, because it depends on the node.

rows.clause: The outer store HashSet of channels: a send adds the channel to the set, a receive uses only the empty pattern, and joins are allowed.
rows.note: A receive fires with the unit, which is Some(()), or it waits. So a process never observes an absent unit (rule HS-6, decision 73).

rows.clause: Inner collections: a pair of collection types replaces the two bags, the collections are unindexed, patterns depend on the collection type, and produces need not commute.
Bags: the multiset semantics of the default space.
Sets: each datum or continuation appears at most once, and a second equal send is idempotent.
rows.note: Equal data form one class (rule ST-2). Two waiters are equal only when their bytes are equal (rule ST-9, item F14 of decision 39).

rows.clause: Cells: at most one datum or continuation on a channel, and a second send is an error.
rows.note: Line 239 notes that exactly one datum would need more machinery. That sentence requires no behavior.

rows.clause: Queues: FIFO semantics, only the heads interact, one queue is empty or the heads do not match, and nodes agree on the arrival order.
Priority queues: a queue for each priority, and patterns can name a priority.
Stacks: FILO semantics, and only the tops interact.
A bag and a vector DB: receives wait in a bag, data goes into a vector DB, a pattern gives a vector and a similarity bound, and a receive takes one vector within the bound.
Look into tensor logic for a vector DB.
rows.note: The design study of decision 52 answered the question. The TensorLogic GSLT and its FLT surface come in phase P12, after the readiness signal of F1r3lang.

rows.clause: Look into nonlinear operations on vectors, such as majority for binary vectors and an elementwise sigmoid.
rows.note: These operations come with tensor logic in phase P12. The five exact operations of rho:lang:vector exist now (example vector-ops).

rows.clause: Other collections: fixed-size versions of the collection types, and collections that mix data types.
rows.reason: Decision 87 records the passage as informative. Its fixed-size versions exist where the legacy branch had them: the size of an Array and the capacity of a VectorDB collection.

rows.clause: Qualifiers change the behavior and the persistence of the channels of a space, and some outer structures, such as sets, require the sequential qualifier.
Pathmaps with quantale semantics require the sequential qualifier.
rows.reason: The clause depends on the quantale semantics of row RR-15, which decision 87 records as informative. A PathMap space takes every qualifier.

rows.clause: The default qualifier: a channel persists, and it allows concurrent access.
The temp qualifier: concurrent access, and the data and continuations of the channel are never written to disk.
rows.note: A temp space lives for one deploy, and the sweep at the end of the deploy removes its state (plan revision I-4).

rows.clause: The seq qualifier: temp, and a seq channel is never sent, is not used in a concurrent process, and is used in at most one sequential process.
The use block sets the default space of untagged channels in new blocks and of forged names.
The introduction of the example: one space on each of n channels, qualifiers that set persistence and sequentiality, and theories that a later design document specifies.
rows.reason: The paragraph introduces the example of rows RR-39 to RR-43. Its sentence on theories is row RR-07.

rows.clause: The factories by URN, the FIPS names rho:space:HashMapBagSpace and rho:space:PathMapSpace included, and their calls with a qualifier and a theory.
Inside a use block, new x : s creates a name in the space s, and a forged name is created in the space of the use block.
Joins are permitted in one space and prohibited across spaces.
rows.note: `join_produce_search_agrees_with_head` is a theorem of the search before decision 118. The GREEDY part of `prop_join_produce_search_agrees_with_head` runs for a non-persistent x only, and the allowed set checks a persistent x.

rows.clause: Inside a new block that creates names in the spaces, the names of the spaces refer to the modified spaces, and outside it they refer to the unmodified spaces.

no_model.reason: The clause is the scoping of a typing context. A name from new is unforgeable and lexically scoped in the baseline, so no new model is needed (decision 77).

rows.note: A space keeps its theory. The new block adds its names to the space, and the names reach only the scope of the block.

rows.clause: getSpaceAgent returns the agent of a space, and assertEqual compares it with the factory.
rows.note: getSpaceAgent replies with the factory capability of the family of the space (decision 9). assertEqual takes a reply name, so its arity is 3 (decision 33).

rows.clause: The issues of the current architecture: ISpace couples the outer structure, the inner structure and the operations.
rows.reason: The section motivates the proposal of the rows RR-45 to RR-50.

rows.clause: Layers 1 and 2 of the proposal: the traits DataCollection, ContinuationCollection and ChannelStore.
rows.note: The traits Discipline and OuterStore separate the inner collection from the outer store. They plan whole operations on the staged view of one space transaction, not on mutable collection objects.

rows.clause: Layers 3 and 4 of the proposal: the qualifier enum, the trait SpaceAgent, and the extension traits for checkpoints and replay.
rows.note: Spaces are not ISpace implementors. Checkpoints, replay and reset stay with the one RSpace of the node, which holds the state of every space.

rows.clause: Layer 5 of the proposal: the bag, queue, set and cell collections, the HashMap and PathMap stores, and a generic RSpace over a store and a matcher.
rows.note: GenericSpace takes the injected matcher of the runtime. A space keeps its counters in records and its state in the one history of the node, not in a history repository of its own.

rows.clause: Layer 6 of the proposal: a factory for each kind of space that creates a space from a qualifier, a theory and more arguments.
Layer 6 of the proposal: a registry that registers space factories at run time and creates spaces by name.
rows.note: The fixed URN table registers the builtin families (rule FA-1). Decision 17 postpones the registration of custom spaces at run time to the follow-up rrs-fu-runtime-space-registration.

rows.clause: The migration path of the proposal in six phases.
rows.note: The campaign runs its phases P0 to P12. It keeps HotStore, the host structs and ISpace unchanged, so the phases 1 to 3 of the proposal do not apply.

rows.clause: Agents emulate objects: a constructor sets up the state of a new instance and returns a reference to it.
The agent block: a replicated receive on the constructor creates this and private, dispatches each message [return, method, args] to its method or to default, and replies bundle+{*this}.
rows.note: The parser desugars the agent block (decision 8), and the reference agent uses it. A native space follows the same protocol: its factory replies bundle+{*this}, and HANDLE_OP dispatches each message.

rows.clause: The method-call sugar: x!y(args) means x!?("y", args) as a receive source, before a continuation and as a final send.

no_model.reason: The parser desugars the sugar (decision 8), and the handle receives the desugared call, so the handle protocol models of row AG-02 apply.

rows.clause: The constructor channel r is fresh, this and return are bound in the method bodies, default sees only this, and a return channel is the first element of args.

no_model.reason: The name rule is a check of the first element of a message, which the tests of the drop rule cover.

rows.clause: Every agent has a default clause, because messages of an unexpected shape can arrive on this.

no_model.reason: The default behavior is one typed reply or one drop for each message, which the tests check.

rows.note: A native handle answers an unknown method with a typed reply and drops a malformed message, as a default clause does. The reference agent has a default clause.

rows.clause: The desugaring binds a private channel for the state of an instance, and the Private Methods FIP builds on it.
rows.note: The private channel belongs to the agent sugar of the parser. A native handle keeps its state in the records of its space, and a user agent may use private.

rows.clause: The constructor composes with the send-return syntax: for (b <- ctor!?(args)) calls methods of b.
